math_contract: grouped per-expert fused gate/up GEMM + activation
description: aiter FlyDSL fused MoE stage-1: the per-expert gate/up projection GEMM (bf16 activation x mxfp4 w1 -> bf16) over the sorted (token,slot) pairs, with the SiTUv2 activation and gate*up multiply fused into the epilogue. Profiled as `moe_gemm1_0` -- 13.53% of e2e-weighted GPU time (99176 calls, 10624.8 ms), the single largest kernel in the Kimi-K3 0828 profile. The live 0828 launch variant is `flydsl_moe1_abf16_wfp4_bf16_t32x64x256_w3_xcd4_kw2`, i.e. out_dtype='bf16' -- stage-1 does NOT fuse the output quantization in this configuration, so the call returns one bf16 tensor and the mxfp4 requant of a2 happens in a separate fused_dynamic_mxfp4_quant_moe_sort call outside this seam.
rebind_seam_note: The live dispatch is AiterRunnerCore.run -> aiter.fused_moe:fused_moe -> fused_moe_2stages -> _flydsl_stage1_wrapper (fused_moe.py:1169) -> aiter.ops.flydsl.flydsl_moe_stage1. A candidate integrates by replacing aiter.ops.flydsl.flydsl_moe_stage1 (package attribute AND aiter.ops.flydsl.moe_kernels.flydsl_moe_stage1) via a PYTHONPATH sitecustomize overlay; the wrapper resolves tile/dtype/swizzle kwargs from get_flydsl_kernel_params(kernelName) and passes the WHOLE set through by keyword, so a replacement must accept the same keyword set (see meta.live_call_kwargs).
pct_gpu_time_note: 0828 cycle1 e2e-weighted: 99176 calls, 10624.76 ms total (prefill 4753.041 / decode_e2e 5871.718), prefill 956.731 us/call, decode 35.12 us/call, phase split prefill 53.5 / decode 46.5.

quant.act_dtype: bfloat16 (stage-1 consumes the UNQUANTIZED hidden states: untuned_fmoe_live.csv q_dtype_a=torch.bfloat16, so a1_scale is None and the kernel takes the a16w4 path)

regime.notes: 0828 cycle1 baseline flags: --chunked-prefill-size 8192, --cuda-graph-max-bs 64, --moe-runner-backend aiter, --trust-remote-code. Decode replays under a HIP graph; prefill runs eager.

tol_note: 0.02 (the default) -- but ONLY because correctness compares the elementwise MEDIAN over 21 independent launches of each leg. A SINGLE launch of this kernel is not reproducible (see nondeterminism_calibration); against a single-launch oracle no tolerance works, because the baseline's disagreement with ITSELF (harness err 27) exceeds the disagreement produced by a real wrong tile config. Medianed, the frozen baseline reproduces itself BITWISE and tol=0.02 still rejects act=silu (err 8.9) and situ_beta=0.5 (err 0.50). Do not raise this; if the median stops being bitwise-stable, raise median_launches instead -- _extract_gen1.py hard-fails on that.
provenance_note: ROUTING IS REAL but SECOND-HAND: it is the served topk distribution captured at the stage-2 seam of the 0817 session (ut_stage2/reference_io.pt, same model / TP=8 / ISL 8192 / OSL 1024 / conc 64), inverted back to (topk_ids, topk_weights) and re-sorted by the production aiter moe_sorting at stage-1's own block size. It was NOT captured at the stage-1 seam. The launch variant is the REAL 0828 one (kernel name recorded live in tuning/work + the architect report), resolved through the frozen registry, but the DECODE variant is assumed identical to prefill's rather than observed. _capture_overlay1/ is the (unrun) hook that would replace both with a first-hand stage-1 capture. SEPARATELY: the golden is the elementwise MEDIAN of 21 frozen-baseline launches, not a single launch, because this kernel is not run-to-run reproducible at served routing spreads -- see nondeterminism_calibration.

nondeterminism_calibration.summary: aiter FlyDSL stage-1 is not run-to-run reproducible once the sorted routing spans more than ~50 expert blocks: ~0.5-1% of output elements differ between consecutive launches on identical inputs, relL2 ~2e-2. Every served bucket except M=1 is in that regime (decode M=64 -> 469 blocks, prefill M=8192 -> 4535 blocks).
ruled_out: operand OOB: guard-padding a (4x), w1 (2x) and w1_scale (4x) changes nothing
output OOB: a guard row appended to `out` stays exactly 0.0, so padded-slot stores ARE masked
routing/padding: moe_sorting pad marker is (topk<<24)|M, 0 pads land inside [M,topk], 0 duplicate (token,slot) pairs
launch knobs: k_wave 2->1, k_batch, xcd_swizzle 4->0, waves_per_eu, b_nt, use_async_copy
call convention: kwargs match aiter/fused_moe.py:_flydsl_stage1_wrapper line for line
weight layout: reproduced with aiter's own recipe (shuffle_weight_a16w4 + shuffle_scale_a16w4); both shuffles are shape-preserving here (688128x112, factor 1.0)
the machine: ut_stage2's UT passes on the same node/GPU/container
the frozen copy: the INSTALLED aiter shows the same behaviour
nondeterminism_calibration.upstream_corroboration: op_tests/flydsl_tests/test_flydsl_moe_a16wfp4.py:_check_result gates this op with cosine similarity + atol=1.0 + pass_pct=95.0, i.e. aiter itself does not treat these outputs as elementwise reproducible.

discriminating_power_at_tol_0.02_via_med.tile_n=256: PASS -- and correctly so: resolve_flydsl_stage1_tile_n downgrades it to 128 and tiling is mathematically neutral. It is a PERF lever, never a correctness control; the NOTES.md lever must be measured in the timing legs, not here.

nondeterminism_calibration.known_limitation: a perturbation confined to a single expert (1 of 896 scales doubled) stays inside the median's residual at the big buckets (relL2 0.039 vs 0.024 floor) and is invisible at M=1 when that expert is unrouted. This UT gates errors that touch a meaningful fraction of experts, not single-expert drift.

scale_calibration.why: e8m0 group scales are drawn near 2^-10, not near 2^0 as in ut_stage2. A real mxfp4 w1 entry has std ~1/sqrt(model_dim); with unit-scale bf16 hidden states and K=3584 that puts the gate/up accumulator at O(1), which is where SiTUv2 operates.
scale_calibration.failure_it_prevents: at scales near 2^0 the SiTUv2 output pins at its +-1 clamp for ~50% of elements, so the kernel's run-to-run spread appears as SIGN FLIPS of magnitude 2.0 -- an oracle no tolerance can gate.
